Workspace stuck in 'Starting' state

The image is usually downloading for the first time, which can take several minutes for big GPU images. If it is still Starting after 10 minutes, ask your admin if your project's plan window is open right now.

Session expired and redirected to login

Sessions expire. Sign in again; your workspaces keep running.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
A group is a team or a course. Members share group storage, and you can add a whole group to several projects.

Who can use it: everyone can belong to a group. Only platform admins create groups. For a new one, send a Request.

docs.title: Group membership model
docs.text:
A group has three roles; your role also sets your default permissions on projects the group owns.

Role Add / remove members Set storage permissions Access group storage Admin ✅ ✅ ✅ Manager ❌ ✅ ✅ User ❌ ❌ ✅

Teaching assistants usually need Admin

Manager can set students' storage permissions but not add or remove members. If you run a course, ask a platform admin for Admin.

docs.title: Groups list page
docs.text:
Figure 1: The groups list, one card per group.

Groups in the sidebar lists every group you belong to. Each card shows the icon, name, description, ID and created date; click it to open the group. Platform admins also see Edit group and Delete group, and set group policies (Storage Policy, Build Registry Lane, Root Containers, Allowed host paths) under Admin → Groups.

docs.title: View a group
docs.text:
• Members: everyone in the group and their roles
  • Storage: the group's volumes and their permissions

docs.title: Requesting a new group
docs.text:
Only platform admins see Create Group. To get a group:

  1. Go to Requests → New Request.
  2. Say what the group is for, who will be in it, and how much group storage you need.
  3. A platform admin creates the group and makes you its group admin.

docs.title: Join a group
docs.text:
You can't browse or search for groups, so ask your team which one to join. Only group admins and platform admins can add members:

  1. Submit a request of type Access.
  2. Say which group you need and why.
  3. A group admin or platform admin adds you.

docs.title: Add members to a group
docs.text:
Requires the group role Admin.

  1. Open the group and click + Add Members (top right of the Members tab).
  2. Search by username or email.
  3. Pick users from the results.
  4. Click Add Members.

To add a whole class, use Paste users: paste the list (separated by new lines, commas, semicolons or tabs) and click Resolve Users.

Results list only people who aren't members yet.

Figure 2: The Add members dialog.

docs.title: Storage permission inheritance
docs.text:
You set group permissions (Read, Write or None) on the group page; projects show them read-only. Each group volume also has an Access Policy, the default for members you haven't set individually.

Key rule: if you are in the group, your permissions on a volume attached to a project always come from the group, and a project can't override them. Project-level grants apply only to project members outside the owning group. The project's storage page shows group-derived permissions as read-only, with a badge linking to the group's permissions page.

Permissions count only for current members, so at the end of a term remove people from the group; you don't need to touch each project.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
I can see a group but can't add members.

Adding members needs the group role Admin. Ask a group admin or platform admin.

Why are my storage permissions greyed out on the project page?

You're in the group that owns this storage, so the group sets your permissions. Open the group's Storage tab to see them.

Can I belong to more than one group?

Yes.

How do I leave a group?

You can't leave on your own. Ask a group admin or platform admin to remove you. You lose the group's storage right away; personal storage is unaffected.

docs.title: Home dashboard
docs.text:
The Home dashboard shows free GPUs, your quota use, your running jobs, and your recent requests.

Who can use it: all signed-in users.

docs.title: Widget reference
docs.text: Widget What it shows Refresh GPU Availability Card Free and used GPU units across the platform, plus a preemptible-queue count On page load and every 10 seconds GPU Cluster Status Anonymous GPU machine cards showing how much of each GPU is in use On page load and every 10 seconds Project count (header line) Number of projects you belong to, and how many of them have a plan On page load and every 10 seconds Resource Usage History GPU/CPU/memory quota used vs. allocated for each project that has a plan, plus plan-window status On page load and every 10 seconds; countdown ticks every second Recent Activity Your 8 most recent requests On page load and every 10 seconds My GPU Jobs Your running GPU jobs with GPU share, memory, and running time On page load and every 15 seconds

docs.title: Reading GPU availability
docs.text:
The GPU Availability Card shows how many GPUs are free right now.

Figure 1: Home dashboard showing GPU availability, resource usage, and active jobs.

  1. Read the allocated / total fraction, for example 6 / 8 GPUs.
  2. Free GPUs = total − allocated. At 0 free, a new workspace waits in line.
  3. The card also shows a Preemptible queues count. When every GPU is busy, higher-priority work can still start by stopping a lower-priority workspace in a preemptible queue.
  4. Admins also see a View Reports button that opens the Audit page.

Effective GPU units

The card counts effective GPU units, not whole cards. One GPU at 50% SM share counts as 0.5 GPU, and only while a workload is using it.

docs.title: GPU cluster status
docs.text:
Below the availability card, the GPU Cluster Status grid shows each GPU machine under an anonymous label:

  • A display label such as GPU node 1 and the GPU model
  • Each physical GPU, with its index and model
  • How many shares of that machine's GPUs are taken, such as 3 / 8
  • A status bar and usage percentage for each GPU

Check it before you submit to see which models are idle and whether a machine has room for a part-GPU claim. Other users' names and workloads are never shown.

docs.title: Resource usage history
docs.text:
The chart shows your usage per project that has a plan. Projects without a plan are not listed; if none has one, a notice appears.

  • Each bar is one project.
  • The fill shows how much quota you have used (GPU hours, CPU hours, or memory).
  • Each project row shows whether its resource plan is always active, closing, opening, or expired.
  • Plan-window countdowns update every second without a refresh.

docs.title: Recent activity
docs.text: The Recent Activity panel lists your 8 most recent requests, with their tag and submit time. Click View All to open the Requests page.

docs.title: My GPU jobs
docs.text:
The My GPU Jobs table lists the GPU jobs (workspaces and deployments) you have running right now. One row is one job; a job that spans several cards is one row.

Column Description Status Always Running; finished jobs are not listed Job The last 8 characters of the job ID Project Owning project GPU Effective GPU share held, and how many cards it touches Memory GPU memory held, in GiB Running How long the job has been running

The table is read-only. Manage workspaces on the Workspaces page and deployments on the project's Resources tab.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Why does the availability card show 0 GPUs?

The card shows effective availability. If every matching GPU or SM share is taken, it shows 0. When a workspace stops, its GPU is free again within about a minute.

Recent Activity is empty. Is something wrong?

No. It lists only requests you sent.

My running workspace is not in the jobs table.

The table refreshes every 15 seconds. If it is still missing after the next refresh, reload the page (F5).

docs.title: Acceptable use
docs.text: These rules apply to everyone with an account. The platform logs activity and access. Role permissions are in Concepts & Roles.

docs.title: Accounts and access
docs.text:
1. Your account is yours alone. Do not give your account, password, API token, VPN profile, or keys to anyone, including lab mates, project partners, and TAs.
  2. When someone else needs resources, ask an admin to create an account for them, or add them to your project or group. Never share a login.
  3. Use a password of at least 8 characters, and not one you use elsewhere. You cannot reset it yourself. Ask an admin, and the new password works for the VPN too.
  4. Treat an API token like a password. Keep tokens out of code, notebooks, images, and Git repositories. Revoke tokens you no longer use under Settings.
  5. Five failed sign-ins lock you out for 15 minutes. Do not script sign-in attempts.
  6. Use the platform through the VPN and cscc.nthu.edu.tw addresses. Do not bypass the VPN or connect straight to other internal addresses or IPs.
  7. Do not send requests as someone else, and do not change projects or groups you are not part of.
  8. If your password may have leaked, you see data that is not yours, or you get a sign-in notice you did not cause, change your password and tell an admin.
  9. When your course ends or you leave the lab or the university, ask an admin to disable your account.

docs.title: Compute resources
docs.text:
1. Resources are for teaching and research. Do not use them for mining, password cracking, proxies or tunnels, or commercial services.
  2. Delete a workspace when you are done. Do not leave a GPU idle to hold your spot. A workspace stops on its own after the idle limit shown under the list.
  3. A GPU desktop lasts at most 8 hours, and one nobody watches for 30 minutes is reclaimed. When it ends, only files in mounted storage stay.
  4. One GPU-hour is one GPU running for one hour, with part of a card counted in proportion. When the budget runs out, new GPU jobs and workspaces are blocked. Running work is not affected.
  5. A GPU claim takes quota as soon as you create it, even before a workload uses it. Delete claims you are not using.
  6. Ask only for the GPUs you need, in the number and model you need.
  7. On a preemptible queue, higher-priority work can stop your workspace. Save progress to mounted storage and make your training resumable.
  8. Do not get around quotas, runtime limits, or scheduling rules. That includes auto-restart scripts and fake activity that stops the idle timeout.
  9. For resources beyond your quota, file a resource request under Requests.

docs.title: Storage and data
docs.text:
1. Only mounted storage stays: personal storage at /home/<your username>, group storage at /mnt/shared/<volume name>. Files saved anywhere else are gone when the workspace stops or is deleted.
  2. Platform storage is not backed up. Keep your own copy of anything you cannot lose.
  3. Stay within your quota. When the usage bar turns amber (70%) or red (90%), clear caches, dataset copies, and old checkpoints before you ask for more.
  4. Do not store files unrelated to teaching or research, such as personal media, personal backups, pirated software, or datasets of unclear origin.
  5. Group storage is shared. Work in your own folders, and do not change or delete other people's files. When you leave the group, you lose access to that volume.
  6. Before you store personal data, an unpublished dataset, or anything you must keep confidential, check its licence and the rules, and get your advisor's OK. Keep such data out of group storage and images.
  7. For files over 500 MB, download them inside a workspace with wget, curl, or rclone. Do not upload them through the browser.
  8. Deleting a storage volume erases its contents for good. Copy your data out before you leave the platform.

docs.title: Images, licensing, and external services
docs.text:
1. Use images from trusted sources. The platform scans images for security problems automatically. The platform refuses an image only when it holds a package that is unsafe to run here, and the job then fails with the reason "blocked by the platform". Known vulnerabilities in your own container do not block it.
  2. Follow the licence of every piece of software, model weight, and dataset you use. Do not install or share pirated or cracked software.
  3. Do not put accounts, passwords, tokens, keys, or unlicensed data in the images you build.
  4. An image a project builds is for that project.
  5. Do not run unapproved services for outside users, such as public websites, file sharing, and proxy nodes.
  6. Do not scan, probe, or attack any machine or service, on or off the platform, including other people's workspaces.
  7. Do not turn off or get around the platform's security controls or logs.
  8. When you publish results, credit the platform's compute the way your institution requires.

docs.title: Questions
docs.text: If a rule does not cover your case, send a problem report under Requests or ask a platform admin.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
A project owns your quota, config files and deployments. Every workspace you start uses a project's quota.

Who can use it: everyone who is signed in. Registering creates your personal project.

docs.title: Project page layout
docs.text:
Figure 1: Projects list in list view, the default.

Switch views with the icons at the top right of the toolbar:

  • List view (default): a table with sortable columns
  • Grid view: cards with the project name, description, member count and GPU usage bar

docs.title: Create a project
docs.text:
Creating a project needs the manage-projects permission. Without it, New Project is hidden; ask an admin to create one for you.

  1. Click Projects in the left sidebar.
  2. Click New Project (top right).
  3. Fill in the project form:
Field Description Name Short identifier (alphanumeric, hyphens allowed) Group Owning group (required) Description Optional. What the project is for
  1. Click Create.

Quota is assigned by an admin

A new project has zero GPU quota. Send a Request to have an admin attach a Resource Plan.

docs.title: Project detail tabs
docs.text:
Everyone sees Overview, Config, Plan, Builds, GPU Claims and Resources. Ray appears when Ray sessions are turned on; Members, Storage and Settings depend on your role.

Figure 2: Project detail tabs.

Tab Contents Overview Description, quota usage chart, GPU-hour budget, current plan, member summary Config Config files under version control: what you want to deploy Plan The project's resource plan, schedule window, allowed GPU models and quota limits Builds The project's image builds: pick an archive or a Dockerfile, see the shared queue and read live build logs GPU Claims GPU reservations you create ahead of time and attach to a deployment later Resources What you run, in one tab per kind (Pods, Services, …), and live GPU, CPU and memory use. Managers also see every member's Ray Your Ray sessions, or the address to submit Ray jobs to. Shown only when Ray sessions are turned on Members / Storage Extra tabs, shown when your role lets you manage members, quotas or storage Settings Limits for every workspace in the project. See Project settings below

The Storage and Settings tabs need Project Manager or above. Only Project Admins see Members (platform admins must switch to Admin View in the avatar menu). An Admin can't demote themselves, so a project always keeps one Admin.

docs.title: Project settings
docs.text:
The Settings tab (Project Manager or above) sets limits for every workspace in the project and holds its Docker Hub connection:

Field What it does Max workspace continuous runtime In seconds. A workspace that has run longer than this is stopped automatically. 0 means no limit (the default). Docker Hub Username and access token for private Docker Hub images. See Use private Docker Hub images below.

Click Save Changes. The limit also applies to GPU desktops from this project.

docs.title: Build project images
docs.text: Use the Builds tab when the project needs its own image. The FROM image can come from any registry; the platform scans it automatically, with no approval step. Project Managers and Admins can start builds when image builds are on for the project. Project Members can see status and logs, and delete the image of a finished build they started, but cannot start builds.

docs.title: Source options
docs.text: Source When to Use It Upload archive Upload a .tar.gz or .zip. Put the Dockerfile at the top level of the archive. Dockerfile only Paste a Dockerfile. The platform sets up the rest of the build for you.

docs.title: Build settings
docs.text:
Field Notes Image Name Short name, for example trainer-api. The platform makes the full registry path. Tag Optional. Leave it empty for the platform default, or use a version like v1.0.1. Build source Upload archive or pasted Dockerfile.

Builds run one at a time from a shared queue. Each gets fixed CPU, memory and scratch space that doesn't count against your quota. The platform checks uploaded archives for unsafe paths and size limits first.

The build engine shuts down when idle, so the next build waits about a minute for it to start.

The build history shows status, source type, destination image and live logs. A failed build shows a short summary; click the log button for the full output. After a retry, the log view keeps the previous failure reason above the current one.

Each build row has icon buttons: Cancel build while it runs (Delete image artifact once it has produced an image), Clear saved logs and Delete history record.

  • Clear saved logs: builders and project managers can clear logs of finished or failed builds. History and images stay.
  • Delete image artifact: the member who started a finished build, or a project manager.
  • Clear my completed build images: deletes every finished image you built in this project. History and saved logs stay. A tag ID that appears more than once is deleted once.
  • Delete history record: removes only the history and saved logs, not the image artifact. The image registry frees the space in its daily garbage collection, and a recently uploaded image may need two runs before it can be removed.

Build access is project-governed

No start form means the project has Image Build Permission off or your role can't start builds. You can still see build history and logs. Ask a project manager or platform admin to change it.

docs.title: GPU Claims
docs.text: The GPU Claims tab lists reservations you create before you deploy; see GPU claims. A config file's claim slot gets a claim in the deploy dialog.

docs.title: Create a claim
docs.text:
Fill in the Create GPU ResourceClaim form and click Create:

Field Notes Claim name The name you use when you attach this claim to a deployment. Letters, digits and hyphens only. GPU device class The GPU model to reserve. The form starts with a specific model. Pick Any only if the model doesn't matter. GPU count How many physical GPUs this claim reserves. A claim with several GPUs is still one reservation. SM share Compute share from 1% to 100%. The effective GPU count shows next to the form. VRAM mode Elastic shares GPU memory with other workloads. Hard cap keeps to the percentage you pick. VRAM share Only used with Hard cap. The memory is worked out from the smallest card of that model.

All replicas of a Deployment share one claim. Quota and GPU-hours count once per claim, not per replica.

An unattached claim uses 0 GPU-hours but still counts against project and per-user GPU quota. Status is Reserved (nothing attached), Allocated (a GPU is assigned) or In use by . You can delete unused claims, not one a running workload uses.

Claim ownership

Project Members can create their own claims. Project Managers can also see and delete other members' claims.

docs.title: Plan window countdown
docs.text:
The Plan tab shows a scheduling and a priority countdown in Taiwan time (UTC+8). Schedule Window decides when work can start; see Plan window.

  • Window closes in HH:MM:SS is how much time you have left.
  • Window opens in HH:MM:SS is when you can start work again.
  • Always active means no weekly schedule limit.

The deploy dialog warns you before scheduling closes. After that you can't start new deployments on any queue; running workloads follow the plan's stop policy.

With Burst Windows, you also see Priority ends in HH:MM:SS or Priority starts in HH:MM:SS. Priority queues appear only where burst overlaps the schedule hours. When burst closes, scheduling stays open and existing work keeps running; see Plan window for deployments still on a priority queue. If a window changes while the deploy dialog is open, it refreshes the queue choices, keeps your selection if still available, and clears old validation results.

An admin can set a runtime limit on a queue. If your queue has one, your workload stops after that many seconds and the bell shows Runtime limit reached. Your config file can't raise or turn it off.

With a GPU-hour budget, Overview shows a GPU-hours bar (used this period vs. budget), the reset period (monthly, weekly, or every N hours) and the next reset (UTC+8). When the budget runs out you can't start new GPU jobs or workspaces until the reset; running jobs continue.

docs.title: Which images a project can run
docs.text:
Images you build are private to the project. A project can run:

  • images it built itself;
  • images of the platform, such as the ready-made IDE and desktop images;
  • public images from Docker Hub, GHCR and NVIDIA NGC, through the platform mirrors;
  • older images built before builds became private to each project: an image you built yourself works only in your personal project, and an image a group built works only in projects that group owns.

An image another project built gives an Error row in Image security checks with Image security check refused: <ref>: built by another project; use this project's images, platform images or public mirrors. Rebuild it in your project, or ask its owner for the Dockerfile. A build whose FROM image belongs to another project is rejected the same way.

docs.title: Use private Docker Hub images
docs.text:
A Project Manager connects a Docker Hub account once for the whole project:

  1. On Docker Hub, go to Account settings → Personal access tokens and create a token with Read-only access.
  2. In the project, open Settings → Docker Hub account, enter the Username and Access token, and click Save. The platform checks them with Docker Hub first and rejects a wrong pair with Docker Hub could not be reached with this username and token.
  3. Use the image as usual: image: <user>/<repo>:<tag> in a job, deployment or workspace, or docker run in the project's IDE.

The section then reads Connected as <username>, updated <time>. The token is never shown again; to change it, save a new one. Remove asks for confirmation, disconnects the account and deletes the project's cached private images. Public Docker Hub images keep working either way. A Dockerfile FROM line can use a private Docker Hub image too.

A member who ran docker login in the IDE has a personal Docker Hub login, which the platform tries before the project account. See Private Docker Hub images.

Private images get the same security check, and only this project can use them. Every member's workloads can pull any private image of that account, so connect an account and token meant for the project.

docs.title: Image security checks
docs.text:
The Overview tab has an Image security checks card listing the last 10 images your project's jobs and workspaces started, with a status for each:

Status Meaning Checking The platform is still checking the image. The card refreshes by itself. Passed The image can run. Failed The platform blocked the image because a package in it is unsafe to run here. Error The check could not finish, for example the image or tag does not exist, or the check timed out. Unsupported The image comes from a registry the platform cannot check.

The platform blocks an image only when it holds a package that endangers the platform. Known vulnerabilities in your own container do not block it. Each row also shows a one-line reason and when the image was last used. When the platform has image checks turned off, the card says Image security checks are turned off.

Click a Failed row to see what to upgrade: each blocking package, your installed version and the version to upgrade to. Vulnerability IDs are not shown; only administrators see them. The other statuses have no details to open.

A Failed row reads: <image>: blocked by the platform because <package> <version> is unsafe to run here. Upgrade it to <fix version> or later (rebuild on a newer base, or pick a newer tag). An Error row can also say the image was not found on Docker Hub, or that its registry is not supported; use Docker Hub, GHCR, NGC or this project's images.

To fix a failure, rebuild on a newer base image tag, or upgrade the listed packages in the Dockerfile (apt, apk, dnf, pip) to at least the fixed version, then run the job again. For a public image, pick a newer tag. For a platform image, choose another version or contact the administrators.

The card shows the latest result per image, and drops the oldest row when an 11th image is used.

docs.title: Config file versioning
docs.text: Every save creates a new version; old versions are kept. You can view or deploy any of them.

docs.title: Working with config files
docs.text:
1. Go to Projects → [your project] → Config tab.
  2. Click New File, then upload a YAML file or paste content in the editor.
  3. Click the History icon next to a config to view all versions.
  4. To deploy a specific version, click Deploy on the version row.
  5. In the deploy dialog, pick the scheduling queue, and a reserved GPU claim for each claim slot in the YAML. The choice applies to this deploy only.

Running instances show in the project's Resources tab, described below.

A finished Pod is removed at most three days after it ends, with its entry and logs in Resources; the logs can vanish sooner (for example when a node restarts). A Job keeps its finished pods until you delete the Job. Save results to a mounted storage volume while the run is going.

docs.title: Containers you can shell into
docs.text:
A Terminal needs a container that keeps running. A bare shell such as command: ["/bin/sh"] exits at once and restarts in a loop, so every terminal attempt fails.

Give the container real work:

command: ["sleep", "infinity"]

or turn on stdin and tty under Interactive shell in the Resource Wizard (stdin: true and tty: true in raw YAML); the wizard warns about a bare shell.

Then open the Resources tab, stay on Pods, and click Terminal on the row. Deployments and Jobs have no button; their running instance is under Pods.

docs.title: Deploy rules
docs.text:
Quota counts everything you already have going, including workloads still waiting to start. Config files can deploy Pod, Deployment and Job; other kinds are rejected.

Every container must set a memory request and limit of at least 128Mi, or deploy and dry-run validation rejects it. Write the unit: a bare memory: "1" means one byte.

docs.title: Asking for a GPU
docs.text:
Two ways to ask for a GPU:

  • Inline GPU request. In the Resource Wizard, pick a GPU model in the container's resource settings. It counts toward your quota and must be a model your plan allows.
  • Reusable GPU claim. In the Resource Wizard, choose Pick at deploy and name the slot, for example train-a. In the deploy dialog, pick one of your GPU Claims for it.

To give a claim to only some replicas, split them into separate Deployments. A config that asks for no GPU needs no allowed-model list and never gets a GPU claim.

Advanced: writing the YAML yourself

Leave the fields the platform manages out of your YAML: don't set metadata.namespace, metadata.generateName, metadata.ownerReferences or metadata.finalizers. For storage, use {{userVolume}} to mount your personal volume. Naming a volume directly works only in a group's project, and only for volumes that group already has.

  • Each pod gets one memory-backed /dev/shm, shared by its regular containers (not init containers), of up to 8 GiB or the pod's memory limit if that is smaller. It is skipped when any container in the pod already mounts something under /dev/shm.
  • An inline GPU request goes straight into the container's resource requests, for example nvidia.com/rtx6000: "1".
  • A GPU claim slot is an annotation on the Pod, or on the Deployment's template: platform-go/dra-claim-name: '{{ gpuClaimName "train-a" }}'. {{gpuClaimName}} with no name still works as the default slot. Two workloads can share a slot deliberately, or use different slots to get different claims.

Config files and deployments require Project Manager role

Only the Manager role or higher can create, edit, deploy, validate, inspect or delete config-file instances.

docs.title: Managing members
docs.text:
1. Open the project and go to the Members tab.
  2. Click + Add Members (you need the Project Admin role).
  3. Search by username or email.
  4. Pick a role for each user:
Role What they can do User Launch workspaces, view configs Manager Edit configs, manage deployments Admin Add/remove members, set member quotas
  1. Click Confirm to save.

Project Admins can tick several rows to remove members, change roles or set per-user quotas in bulk. Managers and Admins see everyone's quota; a Project User sees only their own. A quota of 0 means no per-member limit; the project plan's cap still applies.

Group-inherited members can be part of a bulk quota change, but not a bulk remove or role change; do those in the group.

Removing a direct member also removes their workspace area in the project, storage permission overrides and per-user quota. To remove a group-inherited member, remove them from the group.

docs.title: Group inheritance and effective project role
docs.text:
Your project role in a group-owned project:

  1. If you were added to the project directly, that role wins (admin / manager / user).
  2. Otherwise, on a personal project, the owner counts as admin.
  3. Otherwise, your group role in the owning group. A Group Admin is therefore a Project Admin on every project the group owns, without being added, and can set per-user quotas on the group's projects.

When someone leaves the lab: ask an admin to remove them from the group. They lose every project they joined through it.

docs.title: Deleting a project
docs.text:
Only a platform admin can delete a project, from Admin → Projects. Ask an admin or send a Request, and delete the project's workspaces first. Then:

  • The config version history and deployment records are gone for good.
  • Storage volumes are not deleted. They stay on the Storage page.

docs.title: Resources tab
docs.text:
Your own resources. Cards at the top show your GPU, CPU and memory use. Below them is one tab per kind, each with a count: Pods (opens first), Services, Deployments, StatefulSets, Jobs, ConfigMaps, Secrets, Ingresses, ResourceClaims and RemoteDesktopSessions. Paused jobs sit at the top of Pods, since their Pod is gone until they resume. Delete all removes everything you have in the project and frees its quota.

Everyone's resources. Project Admins, Project Managers and platform Admin/Manager roles get Personal and Members at the top of the tab. Members lists every other member:

Column Meaning User Project member GPU Effective GPU units currently used CPU Requested or observed CPU cores Memory Memory in MiB Pod (the running instance) How many that member has running now

Search by name, or expand a member to see what they run in the same kind tabs. Delete on a member's row removes all their resources and frees their quota. Project Users see only their own resources.

On Pod rows, hover, focus, or tap the status badge for recent events, such as an image pull failure.

docs.title: GPU quota overview
docs.text:
The Overview tab shows a quota bar per resource:

Resource What It Tracks GPU Effective GPU units consumed vs. plan limit CPU CPU cores consumed by running workspaces Memory RAM consumed by running workspaces

At 100% GPU, a new workspace waits in the queue until resources free up.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
I don't see a New Project button.

Only users with the manage-projects permission see it. Ask an admin to create one.

How do I view old config file versions?

On the Config tab, click the clock icon (History) next to a config file. You see every past version with its time.

My project quota is 0 GPUs. How do I get more?

Send a Resource Request through Requests. An admin reviews it and attaches a Resource Plan to your project.

What's the difference between a workspace's GPU and a GPU Claim?

A workspace holds its GPU only while it exists. A GPU Claim is a separate reservation that persists across deployments; use one when several jobs need the same fractional GPU.

Why is the Deploy button disabled?

The project has no active plan, or its schedule window is closed (the default queue doesn't bypass it). The Plan tab shows the next opening.

docs.title: Ray jobs
docs.text:
Submit a Ray job from your laptop with the ray command; the platform starts a Ray cluster on its GPUs, runs the job, and removes the cluster when you stop using it. Code changes need no image rebuild.

Availability

An admin must turn Ray jobs on. If the commands below fail for every project, ask an admin.

docs.title: Submit a job
docs.text:
You need VPN access, a project you belong to, and an API token.

  1. Create an API token under Settings → Security, or with cscc-cli (see CLI and Settings). It is shown only once, so copy it.

  2. Install Ray on your laptop. The version must match the platform's, 2.58.0:

    pip install "ray[default]==2.58.0"

  3. Download the Root certificate from Settings → Security → Downloads and point Ray at it. Without it, ray stops with certificate verify failed:

    export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=~/Downloads/cscc-root-ca.pem
export SSL_CERT_FILE=~/Downloads/cscc-root-ca.pem

    Set both: ray uses the first to submit and the second to follow the output.

  4. Set your token and GPU request:

    export RAY_JOB_HEADERS='{"Authorization":"Bearer cscc_xxx","X-CSCC-GPUs":"2","X-CSCC-Queue":"default-batch"}'

  5. Submit from your code folder. Replace <project id> with the number in /projects/<project id>:

    ray job submit \
  --address https://api.cscc.nthu.edu.tw/api/v1/projects/<project id>/ray \
  --working-dir . \
  -- python train.py

The command uploads your folder, streams the output, and prints the job ID. Run ray job status <job id>, ray job logs <job id> or ray job stop <job id> with the same --address.

docs.title: Choose GPUs
docs.text:
Set these in RAY_JOB_HEADERS. They apply only when the cluster is created; a running cluster ignores them, so wait for it to end to change them.

Each worker has one GPU. Workers start when a job needs them and stop after about a minute without work.

Header Meaning If you leave it out X-CSCC-GPUs Most GPUs (and workers) the cluster may use 1 X-CSCC-Queue Queue the workers run in. Burst queues are not allowed The platform's default X-CSCC-GPU-Model Which GPU model to use The only model your plan and queue allow. If they allow several, the submit fails until you set it

docs.title: What counts against your quota
docs.text:
• While the cluster is open, the GPUs you asked for count against the project's GPU quota and your per-user GPU limit.
  • GPU hours count only running workers.
  • One project holds at most 10 GPU claims at once, so a cluster has at most 10 GPU workers.

If the request does not fit, the submit fails and nothing is created; ask for fewer GPUs or another queue.

docs.title: First submit and when the cluster ends
docs.text:
The first submit starts a cluster, which takes about 30–60 seconds. The command waits up to 2 minutes, then the platform answers 503; run it again. Later jobs on the same cluster start at once.

The platform removes the cluster after either of these:

  • 30 minutes with no running Ray job.
  • A maximum lifetime: your project's maximum job runtime, your queue's runtime limit, or 24 hours, whichever is shortest. A job still running at that point stops.

The next submit starts a new cluster. Anything on the cluster's own disk is gone; keep results in storage (below).

docs.title: See and end your session
docs.text:
In your project, open the Ray tab (shown only when Ray sessions are turned on). Ray sessions lists your open session: status, GPUs held, queue, start time, and Ends by, the latest time it can run. It ends sooner once idle for the time shown under Ends by.

Select End session to stop it now: running Ray jobs stop and the GPUs are released at once. The next ray job submit starts a new session.

With no session open, the section shows this project's --address with a copy button.

docs.title: Keep your data in storage
docs.text:
Every cluster mounts your files like a workspace does:

Storage Path Personal /home/<your username> Group /mnt/shared/<volume name>

Read datasets from and write results to these paths. Your volume permission applies (see Storage).

docs.title: What goes in the upload and what goes in the image
docs.text:
• The upload is your working folder as a zip of at most 500 MiB. .gitignore matches are left out, so list datasets, model weights and virtual environments there, or keep them in storage.
  • Workers run the platform's Ray image, which has NumPy, CuPy, pandas, Ray Tune and Ray Data, but not PyTorch. Large packages are not installed per job; ask for them in a Request for an image.
  • runtime_env downloads (pip, conda, git) need the project's external network access. Without it, put the packages in the image or install them from your storage.

For a complete run, see Use case: sweep hyperparameters across GPUs.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Message Cause and fix 400 X-CSCC-Queue names a queue that does not exist. Check the name. 401 The token is missing, expired or revoked. Create a new one and update RAY_JOB_HEADERS. 403 You are not a member of this project. Check the project number or ask a project manager. 409 or 422 The request breaks a quota or rule: too many GPUs, a queue or GPU model your plan does not allow, a burst queue, or the 10 GPU claim limit. If your plan and queue allow more than one GPU model, add X-CSCC-GPU-Model. The message says which. 422 with a reason The cluster could not start, or the platform rejected the cluster settings. The message gives the reason; no cluster is left running. 503 with Retry-After The cluster is still starting. Run the command again. If it keeps happening for more than a few minutes, ask an admin. Upload fails The folder is over 500 MiB after .gitignore, or the upload took too long. Remove large files.

docs.title: Requests
docs.text:
Ask the admins for GPU quota, storage, group access, a feature, or to report a bug.

Who can use it: all signed-in users.

docs.title: Request types
docs.text: Type When to use it Resource More GPU/CPU quota, more storage, or new resources Access Join a group, use a shared storage volume, or get a higher role Feature Suggest a feature Bug Report a problem Question Ask the admins something Other Anything else

docs.title: Request states
docs.text: State What it means What you can do Pending Sent, waiting for an admin Add details in the message thread Processing An admin is working on it Answer their questions in the thread Completed Done, and the thread is closed Send a new request if you need more Rejected Declined Read the reason and send a new request. An admin can also reopen it

docs.title: Submit a request
docs.text:
1. Click Requests in the left sidebar.
  2. Click New Request (top right).

Figure 1: New request form with request tag, subject, and description.

  1. Fill in the form:
Field Description Project Optional. Links one of your projects so the admins see its GPU quota. Request Tag One of Resource, Access, Feature, Bug, Question, Other. Subject One line, for example "4 GPU units for project LLM-Training". Description Rich text, code blocks, and images (JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WebP, up to 10 MiB each); drag screenshots in.
  1. Click Submit Request. It starts as Pending. There are no drafts.

Say why, how much, how long

For a resource request, give the project, number of GPUs, time period, and research goal.

docs.title: My requests
docs.text:
Figure 2: Requests list with type tags, status badges, and creation dates.

The Requests page lists your requests with who submitted them, tag, status badge, subject, and date. Click one to open its thread; the request page shows the submitter under Submitted by.

docs.title: Message thread
docs.text:
1. Click the request card.
  2. Type in the box at the bottom.
  3. Click Post Reply. Admin replies appear in the same thread.

Figure 3: Request detail page with the message thread.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
How long does review take?

Most requests take 1–2 business days. After three days with no reply, ask again in the thread.

Can I edit or cancel a request?

No. Add or fix details in the thread. Once it is Completed, the thread closes, so send a new request.

My request was rejected. Can I resubmit?

Yes. Send a new one and mention the earlier request number.

I got no notification when my request was resolved.

Turn on Push Notifications under Settings → Notifications.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Edit your profile, change your password, manage API tokens, set notifications and pick a language.

Who can use it: everyone who is signed in. Open Settings in the left sidebar.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
Figure 1: Settings page with the Profile, Security, Notifications, and Preferences tabs.

Tab What you do there Profile Edit your full name; see your username and email Security Change your password; create and revoke API tokens; copy CLI setup commands Notifications Turn notifications on or off; link Discord for direct messages Preferences Choose the display language

docs.title: Profile
docs.text:
• Full Name — you can edit it; it shows wherever your name appears
  • Username — read-only; your sign-in name

  • Email — read-only if your account comes from the school's account directory

  • Open the Profile tab.

  • Edit Full Name.
  • Click Save Changes.

docs.title: Change password
docs.text:
1. Open the Security tab.
  2. Type your Current Password.
  3. Type a New Password (at least 8 characters).
  4. Type it again in Confirm Password.
  5. Click Change Password.

One password everywhere

Your new password works for every sign-in, including the VPN. If your account is managed by an external identity provider, change the password there instead.

docs.title: API tokens and CLI
docs.text:
Get a token for cscc-cli on the Security tab. The table lists active tokens with prefix, last-used time and expiry.

  • Create token — makes a token, optionally named. The dialog shows the full token once and a cscc-cli login --api-url ... --token cscc_... command to paste.
  • Revoke — kills a token; any CLI using it fails on its next call.

A token lasts 90 days by default, and you can have at most 20 active tokens.

Shown once

If you lose a token, revoke it and create a new one.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text:
The Downloads card on the Security tab has the files you install on your own computer. Only signed-in users can download them.

Item What it is cscc-cli for Linux, macOS or Windows The command-line tool. It already trusts the platform certificate SHA256SUMS Checksums to verify a download Root certificate cscc-root-ca.pem, for Python tools such as the ray client

cscc-cli is scanned for known vulnerabilities before each release.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: Checkbox What it does Push Notifications Notifications in the dashboard about your requests and projects. Click Save Changes to save. Email Notifications Shown, but not saved yet. Whether email is sent depends on the platform's mail setup.

docs.title: Discord direct messages
docs.text:
If the Discord bot is on, this tab has a Discord direct messages panel. Click Link Discord and approve on Discord; you return to this page and get a welcome message. The bot then direct-messages you every bell notification, even with the dashboard closed, such as:

  • your workload is about to be preempted, or was preempted
  • one of your jobs finishes or fails
  • a workload is stopped by a runtime limit
  • a burst-window workload moves to normal priority, or stops because none is available
  • new announcements

In the bot chat, /jobs shows 10 jobs per page (Previous, Next). Enter keyword to search job IDs, statuses and queue names, ignoring case; the search persists across pages. active shows running jobs; recent starts with your latest finished jobs. /clear deletes the bot's regular messages; replies marked "Only you can see" stay until you dismiss them in Discord.

Linking also adds you to the platform's Discord server, which the bot needs to message you. If Discord blocks the first message, allow direct messages from server members in your Discord privacy settings, then link again. Unlink stops the messages; the bell keeps working.

docs.title: Preferences
docs.text: Under Language, pick English or Traditional Chinese and click Save.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
The password fields are greyed out.

An external identity provider manages your account. Change the password there.

I forgot my password.

The sign-in page can't reset it. Ask a platform admin to reset it; the new password works everywhere, including the VPN.

My email is wrong.

Your email comes from the account directory. Ask an admin to update it.

Can I delete my account?

Only an admin can. Send a request and say what you need.

I lost my API token. Can I recover it?

No. Revoke it under Security and create a new one.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
A storage volume is a folder that outlives your workspaces.

A workspace with no volume keeps nothing

Personal storage mounts at /home/<your username>; each group volume mounts at /mnt/shared/<volume name>. Files saved anywhere else are lost when the workspace stops, restarts or is deleted. The platform warns you before starting a workspace with no volume.

Who can use it: an admin creates personal storage, so not every account has it; if the My Storage tab is missing, ask an admin. Group admins manage who can use group volumes; only current members can hold permissions.

docs.title: Storage types
docs.text: Personal storage Group storage Owner You A group Created by Admin Admin, on request Who can use it You only Group members, by permission Best for Your datasets, notebooks, experiments Shared datasets, team work Managed from My Storage tab Group Storage tab

docs.title: Storage page
docs.text:
Figure 1: The Storage page with the My Storage and Group Storage tabs.

  • My Storage — your volume as a card with the file browser status (Stopped, Starting, Running, Stopping, Error), a usage bar and the file browser buttons.
  • Group Storage — your groups' volumes in a table: name (with its group underneath; hover for the created date), status (Active is ready to mount, Terminating is being removed, Missing means the platform can't find it; the file browser's state shows below unless it is stopped), usage against capacity (for example 12 / 50 Gi; just the size until usage is measured), your permission, and action icons. The action icons stay at the right edge even when a narrow screen makes the table scroll.

Stopping a workspace doesn't unmount a group volume; it is released only when an admin removes it from the project or deletes it.

If the file browser shows Error, click Start FileBrowser (for a group volume, the icon in Actions) to restart it. Your files are not affected.

docs.title: Usage bar
docs.text:
The bar reads used / total Gi with a percentage. It turns amber at 70% and red at 90%.

Capacity is the space you were given; Usage is what you have written. A dash (—) means not measured yet, not empty. Numbers refresh every few minutes.

docs.title: Volume lifecycle
docs.text:
1. You ask for storage on the Requests page.
  2. An admin approves and creates the volume.
  3. The volume is attached to a project and appears in the workspace form.
  4. Your workspaces, jobs and deployments mount it; data survives restarts.
  5. An admin deletes it, and the data is gone.

Deletion is permanent

Deleting a volume erases everything in it. Back up first.

docs.title: Browse files
docs.text:
1. On the My Storage tab, click Start FileBrowser and wait until the badge shows Running.
  2. Click Open FileBrowser. It opens in a new tab.
  3. When you're done, click Stop FileBrowser.

For a group volume, use the Actions icons: Start FileBrowser, Browse, Stop FileBrowser. They are hidden if your permission is None.

Figure 2: The file browser, with upload, download and delete.

The file browser opens folders, uploads, downloads, creates folders and deletes. Deleting is immediate.

Large uploads

Don't upload files over 500 MB through the browser (size and timeout limits). Download them inside a workspace with wget, curl or rclone.

docs.title: Mount storage in a workspace
docs.text:
1. In the New Workspace form, open Storage Volumes; it lists your personal storage and the group volumes attached to the chosen project.
  2. Tick the volumes you want.
  3. Click Start.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Each group volume has a permission for each user:

Permission What you can do Read Mount and read Write Mount, read, and write None Nothing. You can't mount or browse it

None set by a group admin beats anything the project or group would give you; clear it and your normal permission returns. Ask your group admin to change permissions; they can bulk-edit on the group's Storage tab (see Groups).

Only group managers and admins can open the permissions page; for everyone else the Permissions icon returns to the Storage page.

Your permission applies to everything you run. Without permission, a job or deployment can't mount the volume even if its YAML names it, and a volume not attached to the project can't be mounted from it at all.

Read-only means read-only. With Read, the volume is mounted read-only in every workspace, job and deployment; readOnly: false in your YAML is reset. Project and group managers are no exception.

Separately, jobs and deployments you start from a config file mount group volumes read-only for ordinary project members even with Write; project and group managers skip that rule, but not their own Read.

docs.title: Ask for more storage
docs.text:
Only platform admins create group volumes. To get one, or more space:

  1. Go to Requests → + New Request.
  2. Pick type Resource.
  3. Say what you need: size, purpose and group name.
  4. Click Submit. An admin reviews it and creates the volume.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
My volume shows Pending. When can I use it?

It is still being created, usually under a minute. After 5 minutes, contact an admin.

My volume is full but I see no large files.

In a workspace terminal, run du -sh /home/<your username>/*. The usual culprits are hidden folders such as .cache and .local, and notebook checkpoints.

The usage bar shows a dash.

Not measured yet. Check in a few minutes; if still blank after an hour, contact an admin.

I deleted files but the usage bar has not moved.

Numbers refresh every few minutes. Wait, then reload.

I see a group volume but cannot browse it.

You need at least Read on it. Ask your group admin.

Is my data still there after I delete a workspace?

Yes, unless the volume itself is deleted.

Can several workspaces mount the same volume?

Yes.

Files I uploaded in the browser do not show in my workspace.

Look under /home/<your username> (personal) or /mnt/shared/<volume name> (group). New uploads show up right away; no restart needed.

docs.title: Workspaces
docs.text:
A workspace is a JupyterLab or VS Code environment with GPU access. It starts from one of the platform's images.

Who can use it: project members whose project has enough quota.

docs.title: Workspace states
docs.text:
State What it means What you can do Starting The workspace is downloading its image and starting. Wait 30–120 seconds Running The workspace is ready to use. Open or Delete Stopped The workspace isn't running (for example, it hit the idle limit or the runtime limit). Files in mounted storage are kept. Delete, then create a new one Error The workspace failed to start. Delete, then create a new one

There's no start or stop button; a workspace runs until you delete it or the platform removes it.

docs.title: Workspace list page
docs.text:
Figure 1: The workspace list with status badges.

Each row shows:

  • Workspaces — the workspace name, with the environment and project below it
  • Status — Running (green), Starting (yellow), Stopped (grey), Error
  • Image — the image it runs
  • Resources — the GPU count, or CPU for a CPU-only workspace
  • The last activity time
  • Open (only while Running) and Delete

Below the table, Auto-stop after N minutes of inactivity shows the idle limit (see Idle shutdown).

docs.title: Launch a workspace
docs.text:
1. Click Workspaces in the left sidebar.
  2. Click New Workspace (top-right).

Figure 2: The new workspace form, with project, environment, image, GPU and storage fields.

  1. Fill in the form:
Field Description Project The project this workspace belongs to. It decides which quota you use. Projects without a plan are marked (No Plan) and can't start a workspace. Internet Access Read-only banner: Enabled or Disabled for Internet access. When disabled, the workspace reaches platform services but can't download from outside. Environment JupyterLab or VS Code Image One of the platform's images for that environment: Base Notebook, PyTorch, TensorFlow, CUDA Dev, and their "(Root)" versions. Images you request or build for a project are for deployments, not workspaces. Root shell Makes you root inside your own container. Shown only when the project (and, for a group's project, the group) allows root containers. Scheduling queue One of the queues the project plan allows (see Scheduling queue and priority). GPU How many GPUs. Pick No for a CPU-only workspace. GPU Model One of the models your plan allows. Other models are hidden. Compute quota (%) Share of each GPU's compute. 100% is a full GPU; smaller values count as a fraction. Filled in for a fractional GPU. GPU memory quota (%) Share of each GPU's memory. Follow compute matches the compute quota; turn it off to set your own. Workloads on one card total at most 100%. CPU / Memory Optional. Defaults to the plan's limits Shared memory (/dev/shm) Not a form field. Every workspace gets a memory-backed /dev/shm of up to 8 GiB, or the memory limit if smaller; it counts toward the memory limit. Storage Volumes Tick the volumes to mount. Personal storage is at /home/<your username>; each group volume at /mnt/shared/<volume name>.
  1. Click Start, then wait 30–120 seconds while the status is Starting.
  2. When it is Running, click Open. The IDE opens in a new browser tab.

No storage selected

With no personal storage and no group volume ticked, you see This workspace will not keep your files. Everything you write is lost when the workspace stops, restarts or is deleted. Click Cancel and tick a volume, or I understand, start anyway.

Idle shutdown

A workspace with no activity for the idle limit under the list is stopped, GPU or not. Activity means opening pages, typing in the terminal or running a notebook; an open tab doesn't count. A workspace that is still computing keeps running; a background process using a fraction of a core isn't computing. Delete the stopped one and create a new one; files in mounted storage are kept.

Root shell

Root shell makes you root only inside your own container, with no access to the platform or others' data. No toggle? Ask an admin to allow root containers on the project (and the group, for a group's project).

docs.title: Scheduling queue and priority
docs.text:
Each workspace uses one scheduling queue. Admins set its priority, and whether it is preemptible or has a deserved GPU limit.

Concept Effect on your workspace Higher priority When GPUs are scarce, it's scheduled before workspaces in lower-priority queues. Preemptible queue The platform can stop your workspace to make room for a higher-priority workload. Default queue The lowest-priority queue, used as a fallback. It still needs an active project plan, and the plan must allow it.

The launch form lists the queues the active plan allows; with no plan you can't start a workspace. GPU workspaces are also checked against the models your plan and queue allow, even if you leave the model blank.

docs.title: Plan window
docs.text:
A plan has two weekly windows, in Taiwan time (UTC+8).

Schedule Window is when you can start work. Outside it, Start is rejected on every queue; wait for the next window or ask an admin to update the plan. Running work follows the plan's stop policy.

Burst Windows add priority queues, only while the schedule window is also open. Empty means no priority hours. About 5–6 minutes after a burst window closes, a workspace still on a priority queue is not restarted: it moves to the plan's normal queue for the same GPU model, takes that queue's priority, and can be preempted only if that queue is Preemptible. You get a bell notification. With no normal queue for that GPU model, the workspace is stopped, with a separate notification.

For example, with schedule 09:00–18:00 and burst 13:00–15:00, ordinary queues work 09:00–18:00 and priority queues 13:00–15:00. The project's Plan tab shows both countdowns.

docs.title: Connect to your workspace
docs.text:
When the workspace is Running, click Open; no setup needed.

  • JupyterLab opens at /lab.
  • VS Code Server opens at /.

Both terminals have tmux. A tmux session survives closing the browser tab, not a delete or restart.

Where to save your work

Only files under /home/<your username> (personal storage) or /mnt/shared/<volume name> (group volume) survive the workspace. Everything else is lost on delete.

Use $XDG_CONFIG_HOME, not a hardcoded ~/.config

Workspaces set XDG_CONFIG_HOME=~/.local/config. Tools that follow it (code-server, pip config, gh, …) keep their settings there across workspaces. When you configure a tool by hand, use $XDG_CONFIG_HOME.

docs.title: Stopping a workspace
docs.text: You can't stop a workspace. To free the GPU, click Delete; files in mounted storage are kept.

docs.title: Bulk delete (admins)
docs.text: Admins who manage workspaces can tick several and delete them from the toolbar.

docs.title: How GPUs are allocated
docs.text:
• GPU is how many physical GPUs you ask for.
  • Compute quota (%) is the share that counts toward your quota, shown as Effective GPU.
  • GPU memory quota (%) follows it unless you set your own.
  • Quota counts every workspace you asked for, including ones still waiting to start.
  • Run nvidia-smi to see your GPUs.
  • For a whole GPU or a specific model, pick 100% and a model your plan allows, or ask an admin to change the plan.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
The Open button doesn't appear even though status is Running.

Wait 10 seconds and refresh. If it's still missing, the workspace is probably restarting repeatedly; ask your admin.

My workspace stopped automatically.

It hit the idle limit (see Idle shutdown) or the project's runtime limit. Delete it and create a new one; files in mounted storage are kept.

I see an error status. What do I do?

Delete it and create it again. Usual causes: the image couldn't be downloaded, not enough quota, or the GPU model is unavailable. If it repeats, send a Request.

Can I have multiple workspaces running at once?

Yes, as long as their total GPU use stays within your project's quota.

My workspace was evicted with reason 'Plan window expired'.

The schedule window closed. Create a new workspace in the next window. Burst doesn't get around the schedule. When only the burst window closes, the workspace keeps running on the plan's normal queue for its GPU model.

Why are some GPU models greyed out in the launch form?

The plan hides models it doesn't allow. Ask a project manager to attach a plan with the model you need.

docs.title: 使用案例
docs.text: 每一篇都先在平台上實際跑過，才寫成文章。各功能的說明請看使用指南；cscc-cli 和根憑證在儀表板的設定 → 安全性 → 下載。

docs.title: 大型語言模型推論
docs.text: 文章 內容 用兩張 GPU 跑 14B 模型的 vLLM 服務 單張卡放不下的模型拆到兩張 GPU，用 OpenAI 的 Python 套件呼叫，量每秒產生多少 token

docs.text: 文章 內容 用 config file 在兩張 GPU 上訓練 把 PyTorch DDP 訓練寫成 YAML，從儀表板部署，比較一張和兩張 GPU 的時間

docs.text: 文章 內容 從筆電建置自己的映像 安裝 cscc-cli，在平台上建置映像，再寫進 config file 裡用

docs.title: GPU 桌面
docs.text: 文章 內容 在 GPU 桌面看訓練結果 在瀏覽器開 Linux 桌面，畫出儲存空間裡訓練紀錄的曲線

docs.title: 從筆電建置自己的映像
docs.text:
平台內建的映像涵蓋了常用框架，但專案做久了，總會需要多裝一個套件、鎖定某個版本，或把自己的程式一起包進去。這些都不用在筆電上裝 Docker。cscc-cli build 把資料夾上傳，平台的建置引擎建好映像，存進專案的私有映像倉庫，config file 直接就能用。

這篇建置的映像，就是兩張 GPU 訓練和 GPU 桌面那兩篇用的。跟著做完，你會有：

  • 筆電上裝好並登入的 cscc-cli
  • 一個裝好 PyTorch、TensorBoard、Matplotlib 和你的程式的映像，放在專案的映像倉庫
  • 可以直接寫進 config file 的映像位址

文中的指令和輸出，都是 2026-10-04 在平台上實際跑出來的。

docs.title: 事前準備
docs.text:
• 連得上 VPN，在某個開了 映像建置權限 的專案裡有 管理者 角色
  • 已經有 API token（在設定建立）
  • 大約 15 分鐘

docs.title: 會用到什麼
docs.text: 元件 在哪裡跑 做什麼 cscc-cli 你的筆電 打包資料夾、上傳、即時顯示建置日誌 建置引擎 平台 執行 Dockerfile；全平台一次建置一個 專案映像倉庫 平台 存放映像，只有你的專案看得到

docs.title: 步驟 1：安裝 cscc-cli
docs.text:
登入儀表板，打開 設定 → 安全性 → 下載（說明），下載你系統的檔案。Linux 接著執行：

chmod +x cscc-cli-linux-amd64
sudo mv cscc-cli-linux-amd64 /usr/local/bin/cscc-cli

macOS 用 darwin 開頭的檔案；Windows 見安裝。CLI 已經內建平台的憑證。

用 token 登入，確認身分：

cscc-cli login --api-url https://api.cscc.nthu.edu.tw --token cscc_...
cscc-cli whoami

login 會印出 token 存在哪裡，whoami 會印出你的帳號和角色。

docs.title: 步驟 2：寫 Dockerfile
docs.text:
開一個資料夾，放 Dockerfile 和它要複製的兩支程式：train_ddp.py 和 plot_runs.py。

ddp-trainer/
├── Dockerfile
├── train_ddp.py
└── plot_runs.py

FROM pytorch/pytorch:2.14.1-cuda13.0-cudnn9-runtime

# X11 and Tk so the plots can open in a GPU desktop
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get upgrade -y \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libx11-6 libxext6 libxrender1 libxft2 python3-tk xterm fonts-dejavu-core \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
# The image's Python is system-managed (PEP 668)
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages tensorboard==2.20.0 matplotlib==3.10.7

COPY train_ddp.py plot_runs.py /app/
WORKDIR /app

① apt-get upgrade -y 會補上基底映像的安全性更新，映像第一次啟動前的安全檢查就比較不會擋下它。 ② 這個基底映像把 Python 標成系統管理，pip 要加 --break-system-packages。沒加的話，建置會停在 externally-managed-environment。 ③ 套件都要在建置時裝好，執行中的容器沒辦法 apt-get install。

在資料夾裡執行：

cscc-cli build --project <專案 ID> --name ddp-trainer --tag v1 .

docs.title: 步驟 4：使用映像
docs.text:
Destination 那一行就是映像位址，寫進 config file 的 image: 欄位：

image: 192.168.110.1:30003/p26000001/ddp-trainer:v1

用 config file 在兩張 GPU 上訓練部署的就是這個映像。

docs.title: 成果
docs.text:
筆電上不用裝 Docker，映像在平台上建好，只有你的專案拉得到。之後：

  • 改了 Dockerfile 就換一個 --tag 重新建置，舊的 tag 留給還在用它的 config file。
  • 建置時要帶的值用 --build-arg KEY=VALUE 傳（說明）。
  • 用 cscc-cli build --follow=false 送出後就能關掉終端機，建置歷史在儀表板上看得到。

docs.title: 用 config file 在兩張 GPU 上訓練
docs.text:
訓練在 notebook 裡跑通之後，通常不會一直留在 notebook。程式寫好之後，你會希望它自己跑、能用不只一張 GPU、結果也留得下來。Config file 就是做這件事的：幾行 YAML，平台把它排成一個工作，掛上你的儲存空間，給它方案允許的 GPU。下面這次實測，用 PyTorch DistributedDataParallel（DDP）在兩張 RTX 5090 上訓練 ResNet-18，速度是一張的 1.4 倍，準確率一樣。

這篇用 DDP 在 CIFAR-10 上訓練 ResNet-18，先用一張 GPU，再用兩張。跟著做完，你會有：

  • 一支 DDP 訓練程式，工作分到幾張 GPU 就用幾張
  • 從儀表板部署的 config file，一張和兩張 GPU 各一份
  • 存在儲存空間的 TensorBoard 日誌、模型檔，以及一張 GPU 和兩張 GPU 的實測比較

文中的指令和輸出，都是 2026-10-04 在平台上實際跑出來的。

docs.title: 事前準備
docs.text:
• 在某個專案有 管理者 角色，專案裡有能用 2 張 GPU 的佇列
  • 從筆電建置自己的映像建好的 ddp-trainer 映像，或任何裝了 PyTorch 的映像
  • 大約 15 分鐘

docs.title: 會用到什麼
docs.text: 元件 在哪裡跑 做什麼 Config file 專案的 配置 分頁 描述工作：映像、指令、CPU、記憶體、GPU、儲存空間 torchrun 工作的容器 每張 GPU 啟動一個訓練程序 train_ddp.py 每個程序 各自算每一批資料的一部分，DDP 負責平均梯度 /workspace 你的儲存空間 CIFAR-10、TensorBoard 日誌、模型檔

docs.title: 步驟 1：寫訓練程式
docs.text:
上一篇建好的映像裡，這支程式已經放在 /app/train_ddp.py：

"""Train ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 with DistributedDataParallel.

Launch with torchrun; every process drives one GPU. Rank 0 writes
TensorBoard logs and checkpoints under --out.
"""
import argparse
import os
import time

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import torchvision
import torchvision.transforms as T
from torch.nn.parallel import DistributedDataParallel as DDP
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, DistributedSampler
from torch.utils.tensorboard import SummaryWriter


def loaders(data_dir, batch_size, rank):
    norm = T.Normalize((0.4914, 0.4822, 0.4465), (0.2470, 0.2435, 0.2616))
    train_tf = T.Compose([T.RandomCrop(32, padding=4), T.RandomHorizontalFlip(), T.ToTensor(), norm])
    if rank == 0:  # one download, the other ranks wait at the barrier
        torchvision.datasets.CIFAR10(data_dir, train=True, download=True)
        torchvision.datasets.CIFAR10(data_dir, train=False, download=True)
    dist.barrier()
    train = torchvision.datasets.CIFAR10(data_dir, train=True, transform=train_tf)
    test = torchvision.datasets.CIFAR10(data_dir, train=False, transform=T.Compose([T.ToTensor(), norm]))
    sampler = DistributedSampler(train)
    train_dl = DataLoader(train, batch_size, sampler=sampler, num_workers=6, pin_memory=True, persistent_workers=True)
    test_dl = DataLoader(test, 1000, num_workers=2)
    return train_dl, test_dl, sampler


def accuracy(model, test_dl, device):
    model.eval()
    correct = 0
    with torch.no_grad(), torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
        for x, y in test_dl:
            correct += (model(x.to(device)).argmax(1) == y.to(device)).sum().item()
    model.train()
    return correct / len(test_dl.dataset)


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--data", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=10)
    p.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=256, help="per GPU")
    args = p.parse_args()

    dist.init_process_group("nccl")
    rank, world = dist.get_rank(), dist.get_world_size()
    device = torch.device("cuda", int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
    torch.cuda.set_device(device)

    train_dl, test_dl, sampler = loaders(args.data, args.batch_size, rank)
    model = torchvision.models.resnet18(num_classes=10).to(device, memory_format=torch.channels_last)
    model = DDP(model, device_ids=[device.index])
    lr = 0.1 * args.batch_size * world / 256  # linear scaling rule
    opt = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=lr, momentum=0.9, weight_decay=5e-4, nesterov=True)
    sched = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.OneCycleLR(opt, lr, epochs=args.epochs, steps_per_epoch=len(train_dl))
    loss_fn = torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    writer = SummaryWriter(os.path.join(args.out, f"gpus{world}")) if rank == 0 else None

    for epoch in range(args.epochs):
        sampler.set_epoch(epoch)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        start = time.time()
        for x, y in train_dl:
            x = x.to(device, non_blocking=True, memory_format=torch.channels_last)
            y = y.to(device, non_blocking=True)
            with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
                loss = loss_fn(model(x), y)
            opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            loss.backward()
            opt.step()
            sched.step()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        seconds = time.time() - start
        if rank == 0:
            acc = accuracy(model.module, test_dl, device)
            imgs = len(train_dl.dataset) / seconds
            writer.add_scalar("train/loss", loss.item(), epoch)
            writer.add_scalar("test/accuracy", acc, epoch)
            writer.add_scalar("throughput/images_per_sec", imgs, epoch)
            print(f"epoch {epoch + 1}/{args.epochs}  loss {loss.item():.3f}  "
                  f"test acc {acc:.3f}  {seconds:.1f}s  {imgs:.0f} img/s", flush=True)
    if rank == 0:
        torch.save(model.module.state_dict(), os.path.join(args.out, f"resnet18-gpus{world}.pt"))
        writer.close()
    dist.destroy_process_group()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

① DistributedSampler 讓每個程序拿到不同的一份資料，兩張 GPU 合起來，每個 epoch 每張圖剛好看一次。 ② 學習率跟著 GPU 數放大（0.1 × batch × GPU 數 / 256），因為實際的 batch 也變大了。 ③ 只有 rank 0 下載資料、寫日誌、存模型，其他程序在 dist.barrier() 等它。

docs.title: 步驟 2：寫 config file
docs.text:
打開 專案 → [你的專案] → 配置，按 新增檔案，貼上下面的內容，存成 ddp-gpus2.yaml：

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: ddp-resnet18-gpus2
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        platform-go/dra-gpu-model: rtx5090
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
        - name: train
          image: 192.168.110.1:30003/p26000001/ddp-trainer:v1
          command: ["torchrun", "--nproc_per_node=2", "/app/train_ddp.py",
                    "--data", "/workspace/cifar10", "--out", "/workspace/ddp-runs",
                    "--epochs", "15"]
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "16"
              memory: 48Gi
              nvidia.com/gpu-dra: "2"
            limits:
              cpu: "16"
              memory: 48Gi
              nvidia.com/gpu-dra: "2"
          volumeMounts:
            - name: storage
              mountPath: /workspace
      volumes:
        - name: storage
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: "{{userVolume}}"

① platform-go/dra-gpu-model 標籤和 nvidia.com/gpu-dra 數量，就是在 資源精靈 選 GPU 型號和張數時它寫進去的兩行。部署對話框從這個標籤讀出 GPU 型號。 ② CPU 和記憶體跟著 GPU 數加倍。每個訓練程序開 6 個讀資料的 worker，兩張 GPU 只給 8 顆 CPU 的話，GPU 會一直在等資料。 ③ {{userVolume}} 把你的個人儲存空間掛在 /workspace，資料和結果在工作結束後都還在。

一張 GPU 的版本另存成 ddp-gpus1.yaml：名稱改成 ddp-resnet18-gpus1，--nproc_per_node=1、nvidia.com/gpu-dra: "1"，CPU 8 顆、記憶體 24Gi。

docs.title: 步驟 3：部署
docs.text:
在檔案的版本列按 部署，選佇列後確認。工作會出現在 資源 → Pods，打開它的日誌就能看訓練進度：

epoch 1/15  loss 1.601  test acc 0.462  2.1s  23773 img/s
epoch 2/15  loss 1.469  test acc 0.506  1.5s  32684 img/s
epoch 3/15  loss 1.008  test acc 0.559  1.5s  33115 img/s
…
epoch 13/15  loss 0.448  test acc 0.803  2.0s  25552 img/s
epoch 14/15  loss 0.411  test acc 0.816  1.6s  30847 img/s
epoch 15/15  loss 0.433  test acc 0.821  1.6s  30897 img/s

映像第一次啟動前會先掃描已知漏洞，所以第一次會在這一步等幾分鐘，之後就直接啟動。第一次執行也會把 CIFAR-10（170 MB）下載到 /workspace/cifar10。

docs.title: 步驟 4：比較一張和兩張 GPU
docs.text:
用同樣的方式部署 ddp-gpus1.yaml。兩次都訓練 15 個 epoch：

GPU 數 訓練時間 每秒張數 測試準確率 1 35.7 秒 21,230 82.7% 2 24.9 秒 30,530 82.1%
  • 兩張 GPU 的速度是一張的 1.4 倍，準確率的差距在每次訓練本來就會有的誤差內。
  • 沒有快到 2 倍，是因為 ResNet-18 處理 32×32 的小圖，一步只要幾毫秒。每一步還是要在 CPU 上讀圖、做資料增強，再在 GPU 之間平均梯度，這些成本不會因為多一張 GPU 變少。模型越大、圖越大，每一步花在 GPU 上的時間比例越高，就越接近 2 倍。

每次訓練都會在 /workspace/ddp-runs/ 底下留一個資料夾（gpus1/、gpus2/），裡面是 TensorBoard 日誌，還有 resnet18-gpus2.pt 這樣的模型檔。在 GPU 桌面看訓練結果會把它們畫出來。

docs.title: 成果
docs.text:
你用一份 YAML 描述訓練，佇列允許幾張 GPU 就能用幾張，每次的日誌和模型都留在儲存空間。換成你自己的模型：

  • 把 train_ddp.py 的資料集和模型換掉，DistributedSampler、DDP(...) 和 rank 0 的判斷都留著。
  • 要加 GPU，只改 GPU 數、--nproc_per_node，以及 CPU 和記憶體。
  • 工作跑完後，刪掉它的執行個體，列表上那一筆就會移除。/workspace 裡的檔案都還在。

docs.title: 用兩張 GPU 跑 14B 模型的 vLLM 服務
docs.text:
Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct 是很好用的開源模型，但用 16 位元精度載入，光權重就要 28 GB 左右。RTX 5090 只有 32 GB，放完權重，就沒剩空間給 KV cache（每段對話都要用到的那塊記憶體）。張量平行（tensor parallelism）把每一層拆到兩張 GPU 上，每張卡只放一半權重，剩下的記憶體都能拿來當 cache。下面這次實測，vLLM 在兩張 RTX 5090 上同時處理 64 個請求，每秒產生 2,625 個 token；只用一張卡的話，服務根本起不來。

這篇從工作區啟動模型服務，再用 OpenAI 的 Python 套件呼叫它。跟著做完，你會有：

  • 存在群組儲存空間的模型權重，下載一次，之後每次開服務都能重複用
  • 一個跑在兩張 GPU 上、介面和 OpenAI API 相容的 vLLM 服務
  • 單一請求和同時 64 個請求的實測速度，還有一張 GPU 為什麼跑不起來的實測結果

文中的指令和輸出，都是 2026-10-04 在平台上實際跑出來的。

docs.title: 事前準備
docs.text:
• 專案裡有能用 2 張 GPU 的佇列，並綁定一個還有約 35 GB 空間的群組儲存空間（見儲存空間）
  • 在這個專案開一個工作區，勾選那個群組儲存空間；工作區本身不需要 GPU
  • 大約 30 分鐘，大部分花在第一次下載

docs.title: 會用到什麼
docs.text: 元件 在哪裡跑 做什麼 工作區 平台 你的終端機：下載模型、啟動和呼叫服務 vLLM 服務 獨立的工作，佔 2 張 GPU 每張 GPU 載入每一層的一半，回應 OpenAI API 呼叫 models/ 群組儲存空間 29.5 GB 的權重，所有服務和實驗室成員共用

docs.title: 步驟 1：把模型下載到群組儲存空間
docs.text:
先用 df -h /home/<你的使用者名稱> /mnt/shared/<儲存空間名稱> 看剩多少空間。這次個人儲存空間只有 10 GiB，放不下這個模型，所以放到群組儲存空間，實驗室其他人也能直接用。在工作區的終端機執行：

pip install --user "huggingface_hub[hf_xet]==1.32.0"
export PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH
hf download Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct --local-dir /mnt/shared/<儲存空間名稱>/models/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct

模型總共 29.5 GB，分成八個檔案。工作區中途重啟也沒關係，再跑一次同樣的指令，會從中斷的地方接著下載。

docs.title: 步驟 2：在兩張 GPU 上啟動服務
docs.text:
工作區裡有 docker 指令，可以在工作區旁邊啟動容器（見在 IDE 裡使用 docker）：

docker run -d --keep --name qwen14b --gpus 2 --cpus 8 -m 48g --shm-size 8g \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /mnt/shared/<儲存空間名稱>/models:/models:ro \
  -e HOME=/tmp \
  vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 \
  --model /models/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct --served-model-name qwen2.5-14b \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192

① --keep --gpus 2 從專案配額另外拿兩張 GPU 給容器。工作區本身沒有 GPU，沒有卡可以分給容器。 ② -p 8000:8000 把 API 開在工作區裡的 127.0.0.1:8000。 ③ -v …:/models:ro 用唯讀方式掛權重，服務不可能弄壞共用的那份。 ④ -e HOME=/tmp 讓 vLLM 把編譯快取放在容器裡，不寫到家目錄。 ⑤ --tensor-parallel-size 2 把每一層拆到兩張 GPU 上。

用 docker logs -f qwen14b 看啟動過程，重點是這幾行：

Model loading took 13.93 GiB memory and 47.540906 seconds
GPU KV cache size: 149,488 tokens, Maximum concurrency for 8,192 tokens per request: 18.25x
init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model) took 176.75 s (compilation: 20.35 s)
Application startup complete.

每張 GPU 放 13.93 GiB，剛好是一半的權重。其餘記憶體拿來當 cache，放得下 149,488 個 token，夠 18 段最長的對話同時跑。這次從 docker run 到服務可用花了 8 分鐘，其中 2 分 42 秒是映像的安全檢查和第一次下載，之後再啟動就不用等這段。

CONTAINER ID      IMAGE                      COMMAND                  CREATED         STATUS         PORTS                      NAMES
JOB261004001569   vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0   "--model /models/Qwe…"   8 minutes ago   Up 5 minutes   127.0.0.1:8000->8000/tcp   qwen14b

docs.title: 步驟 3：呼叫模型
docs.text:
服務的介面和 OpenAI API 一樣，官方套件只要改 base URL 就能用。在工作區存成 bench.py：

"""Ask the vLLM server one question, then measure throughput under load.

Usage: python bench.py [concurrent requests]
"""
import asyncio
import sys
import time

from openai import AsyncOpenAI

client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", api_key="unused")
MODEL = "qwen2.5-14b"


async def ask(prompt, max_tokens=256):
    r = await client.chat.completions.create(
        model=MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        max_tokens=max_tokens, temperature=0.7)
    return r.choices[0].message.content, r.usage.completion_tokens


async def main(n):
    start = time.time()
    answer, tokens = await ask("用三句話解釋什麼是 tensor parallelism。")
    print(f"{answer}\n-- {tokens} tokens in {time.time() - start:.2f}s\n")

    prompts = [f"Write a short story about GPU number {i}." for i in range(n)]
    start = time.time()
    results = await asyncio.gather(*(ask(p) for p in prompts))
    seconds = time.time() - start
    total = sum(t for _, t in results)
    print(f"{n} concurrent requests: {total} tokens in {seconds:.1f}s = {total / seconds:,.0f} tokens/s")


asyncio.run(main(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 64))

pip install --user openai==2.8.1
python bench.py 1
python bench.py 64

Tensor parallelism是一種在深度學習模型訓練中分發計算和數據的方法，它將大型張量（多維數組）分割成更小的部分，並在不同的處理器或設備上並行處理這些部分。這種技術可以加速模型的訓練過程並允許使用更大的模型和數據集。
-- 68 tokens in 1.01s

1 concurrent requests: 256 tokens in 2.9s = 88 tokens/s
…
64 concurrent requests: 16384 tokens in 6.2s = 2,625 tokens/s

docs.title: 結果
docs.text:
設定 結果 2 張 GPU，1 個請求 每秒 88 個 token 2 張 GPU，同時 64 個請求 每秒 2,625 個 token 1 張 GPU 啟動失敗：No available memory for the cache blocks
  • 一次只送一個請求，GPU 大部分時間都閒著。vLLM 會把同時進來的請求合在一起算，所以同時送 64 個請求時，每秒產生的 token 數是單一請求的 30 倍。
  • 只用一張 GPU 時，同樣的指令改成 --gpus 1、拿掉 --tensor-parallel-size，載入 27.57 GiB 權重後就停了，已經沒有記憶體可以給 KV cache。在這種卡上，這個模型一定要兩張 GPU 才跑得起來。

docs.title: 步驟 4：停止服務
docs.text:
加了 --keep 的容器在工作區停掉後還會繼續佔著 GPU，而且算進專案的工作數上限和 GPU 時數。用完就刪掉：

docker rm -f qwen14b

權重還留在群組儲存空間，下次啟動不用再下載。

docs.title: 成果
docs.text:
你做出了一個和 OpenAI API 相容的 14B 模型服務，拆在兩張 GPU 上跑，權重只存一份給整個實驗室用。接下來可以：

  • 在工作區裡，把 OpenAI 套件、LangChain 或 LlamaIndex 的 API 位址指到 http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1。
  • 方案允許四張 GPU 的話，用 --gpus 4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 試更大的模型。
  • 只拿得到一張 GPU 時，改用量化過的版本（例如 AWQ）。
  • vLLM 版本固定下來；換新的 tag，第一次啟動要等它的安全檢查。
